function.arguments:
{"path": "plot_codegen.py", "content": """"
HumanEval pass@1 Rate Comparison: CodeLlama vs GPT-4 Across Programming Languages

This script generates a bar chart visualization comparing code generation performance
across 5 programming languages, highlighting the widening performance gap for less
common languages like Rust.
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# HumanEval pass@1 rates (%) for CodeLlama and GPT-4
languages = ['Python', 'JavaScript', 'Java', 'C++', 'Rust']
codellama_scores = [62.3, 55.8, 51.2, 48.7, 31.4]
gpt4_scores = [87.1, 79.4, 74.6, 72.1, 58.3]

# Calculate performance gaps
gaps = [gpt4 - codellama for gpt4, codellama in zip(gpt4_scores, codellama_scores)]

# Set up the figure and axis
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 7))

# Bar width
bar_width = 0.35

# Bar positions
x = np.arange(len(languages))

# Create bars for CodeLlama and GPT-4
bars1 = ax.bar(x - bar_width/2, codellama_scores, bar_width, 
               label='CodeLlama', color='#1f77b4', edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2)
bars2 = ax.bar(x + bar_width/2, gpt4_scores, bar_width, 
               label='GPT-4', color='#ff7f0e', edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2)

# Add value labels on top of each bar
for bars in [bars1, bars2]:
    for bar in bars:
        height = bar.get_height()
        ax.annotate(f'{height:.1f}%',
                    xy=(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, height),
                    xytext=(0, 3),  # 3 points vertical offset
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Customize the chart
ax.set_xlabel('Programming Language', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('pass@1 Rate (%)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('HumanEval pass@1 Rate Comparison:\nCodeLlama vs GPT-4 Across Programming Languages', 
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(languages, fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.legend(fontsize=11, loc='upper left')
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# Add performance gap annotations for each language
gap_positions = [(i, (codellama_scores[i] + gpt4_scores[i]) / 2) for i in range(len(languages))]
for i, (pos_x, pos_y) in enumerate(gap_positions):
    gap = gaps[i]
    # Highlight larger gaps with different styling
    if gap > 20:
        ax.annotate(f'Gap: {gap:.1f}%',
                    xy=(pos_x, pos_y),
                    xytext=(0, 0),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9,
                    color='red', fontweight='bold',
                    bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#ffcccc', alpha=0.5))
    else:
        ax.annotate(f'Gap: {gap:.1f}%',
                    xy=(pos_x, pos_y),
                    xytext=(0, 0),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9,
                    color='darkred', fontweight='bold')

# Add emphasis text for Rust
ax.annotate('⚠️ Widening Gap for Less Common Languages',
            xy=(0.5, 0.95), xycoords='axes fraction',
            ha='center', va='top', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.5', facecolor='#fff3cd', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='#ffc107'))

# Add detailed note about Rust
ax.annotate('Rust shows the largest performance gap (26.9%),\nindicating CodeLlama struggles more with less common languages.',
            xy=(0.5, 0.05), xycoords='axes fraction',
            ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.5', facecolor='#e8f5e9', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='#4caf50'))

# Adjust layout and save
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('codegen_comparison.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
print("Plot saved as 'codegen_comparison.png'")

# Also print summary statistics
print("\n" + "="*60)
print("HUMANEVAL PASS@1 RATE SUMMARY")
print("="*60)
print(f"{'Language':<15} {'CodeLlama':>12} {'GPT-4':>12} {'Gap':>10}")
print("-"*60)
for lang, cl, g4, gap in zip(languages, codellama_scores, gpt4_scores, gaps):
    print(f"{lang:<15} {cl:>11.1f}% {g4:>11.1f}% {gap:>9.1f}%")
print("="*60)
print(f"\nAverage Gap: {np.mean(gaps):.1f}%")
print(f"Max Gap (Rust): {max(gaps):.1f}%")
print(f"Min Gap (Python): {min(gaps):.1f}%")
print("="*60)"}

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

function.name: find
function.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

function.name: workflow_plan
function.description: Register a hierarchical workflow plan. Provide 3-5 main steps at the top level with description, outputFiles, verifiers, and optional children.

function.name: ask_user_question
function.description: Ask the operator a structured question and wait for the answer.
